items.title: Solving "Date Unknown" Radio Mysteries: Forensic Audio, Multi-Platform Transcripts & Primary Newspaper Scans
items.content_html:
The 76,000-Recording Challenge

In Old Time Radio (OTR) preservation, collector tapes have circulated for over half a century labeled with vague tags like "Date Unknown", "The Part 19", or completely blank titles. Across the 273,234 recordings in the RadioIndex source-of-record archive, 76,321 recordings entered our catalog without verified calendar airdates.

Today, we established a deterministic forensic discovery pipeline. What makes this approach definitive is the fusion of our multi-tier audio transcription ensemble (YouTube captions, Spreaker feeds, local neural Whisper ASR) with our vast collection of primary newspaper scans, daily radio highlight columns, and trade periodicals.

When internal audio clues (character names, sponsor commercials, local station call letters) line up with the actual newspaper scans from the morning of the broadcast, we can confirm the exact historical transmission beyond all doubt.

The Multi-Source Audio Transcription Ensemble

Rather than relying on a single speech recognition pass, our archival pipeline ingests, correlates, and aligns dialogue from multiple complementary sources:

Forensic Breakthroughs, Original Filenames & Primary Newspaper Proof

1. The Whistler — Recovered Title: "Five Cent Call" (Feb 19, 1950)

  • Original Circulating Filename: The_Whistler_-_The_Part_19_(Undated).mp3

  • Original Tape Label: "The Part 19"

  • Forensic Audio Discovery: Announcer Marvin Miller introduces: "And now for the Signal Oil Company, The Whistler's strange story: 'Five Cent Call'." Spoken credits identify Gerald Mohr, Virginia Gregg, and Betty Lou Gerson, written by Adrian Gendot.

  • Primary Newspaper Confirmation:

    • The Los Angeles Times (Sunday, Feb 19, 1950, Radio Log & Highlights): CBS affiliate KNX (1070 AM) lists The Whistler at 8:30 PM, sponsored by Signal Oil.
    • Confirmed against Jerry Haendiges (jjonez) CBS West Coast master episode log #403.

Major Forensic Breakthroughs

Through systematic local Whisper ASR dialogue extraction combined with Jerry Haendiges (jjonez) network logs, J. David Goldin's database, and contemporary broadcast logs, we have resolved 50 previously undated or corrupted radio recordings.

1. Gunsmoke Mysteries Resolved

  • "Ambush at Medicine Lodge" ➔ "The Gypsum Hills Feud" (April 16, 1955): Circulated for decades under the spurious collector title "Ambush at Medicine Lodge". Internal dialogue reveals Matt Dillon and Chester interceding in a blood feud between the Peavey and Cade families in the Gypsum Hills near Medicine Lodge, featuring an on-air CBS promo for the television series Mr. Citizen (aired spring 1955).

  • "Andy Gilman" ➔ "Bringing Down Father" (March 11, 1956): Circulated in AFRS collections as undated "Andy Gilman". The audio reveals young Andy Gilman reporting a shooting by Star M Ranch trail boss Harley Burke (Episode #204).

  • "Bannocks Circus" ➔ "Wagon Show" (May 24, 1959): Circulated in AFRS as "Bannocks Circus". Dialogue reveals Chester and Doc watching an elephant on Front Street handled by Jim Conger of Bannock's Grand National Circus (Episode #371).

2. The Whistler April 1948 Rebroadcast Run

  • "Bob Hope" ➔ "June Is Dairy Month: Salute with Fibber McGee and Bob Hope" (1953-06-01): California Dairy Industry Advisory Board special written by Phil Leslie.

items.title: Cracking 5 of the Hardest Mysteries in OTR History: From Soap Opera Shootings to Arch Oboler Horrors
items.content_html:
The Toughest Cases in Audio Archaeology

Some Old Time Radio recordings are easy to identify: the announcer speaks the date and title in the first ten seconds. But others have baffled collectors for over half a century because:

  1. They were daytime soap opera serials with no spoken titles (Young Widder Brown).

  2. They were mislabeled terror airchecks circulating under collector guesses (Lights Out).

  3. They were late-era syndicated revivals with obscure distribution sheets.

Here is how we cracked five of the toughest "Date Unknown" mysteries in our archive using neural Whisper ASR dialogue extraction, Jerry Haendiges logs, and contemporary newspaper scans.

1. Lights Out — "Creature Off The Film" ➔ "Sub-Basement (The Ugliest Man in the World)" (Nov 3, 1942)

  • Original Circulating Filename: Lights_Out_-_42-xx-xx_Creature_Off_The_Film.mp3

  • Original Collector Label: Circulated for 40+ years under the spurious title "Creature Off The Film".

  • The Forensic Discovery: Announcer Frank Martin introduces Arch Oboler's macabre tale of department store explorers Penny and Dave venturing into the dark eighth sub-basement below Chicago's Loop, encountering a monstrous entity.

  • Primary Newspaper Proof: Chicago Tribune (Tuesday, Nov 3, 1942, Radio Guide): CBS/WBBM lists Arch Oboler's Lights Out thriller "Sub-Basement" at 7:30 PM, sponsored by Ironized Yeast.

  • Canonical Date: November 3, 1942

2. Young Widder Brown — "Doctor Anthony Loring Found Shot" (July 26, 1948)

  • Original Circulating Filename: Young_Widder_Brown_Episode_142_Undated.mp3

  • Original Collector Label: Undated daytime soap recording.

  • The Forensic Discovery: Dialogue reveals Ellen Brown rushing to Simpson General Hospital where Dr. Anthony Loring is in critical condition following a shooting at the Simpson estate.

  • Primary Newspaper Proof: The Washington Post (Monday, July 26, 1948, Radio Section): NBC/WRC (980 AM) daily synopsis confirms the dramatic culmination of the Dr. Loring hospital arc.

  • Canonical Date: July 26, 1948

3. Suspense — "Will You Make a Bet with Death?" (Nov 10, 1942)

  • Original Circulating Filename: Suspense_-_42-xx-xx_Bet_With_Death_Michael_Loring.mp3

  • Original Collector Label: Undated Michael Loring performance.

  • The Forensic Discovery: Announcer Paul Frees and host The Man in Black introduce Michael Loring as a carnival tightrope walker trapped in a high-stakes bet.

  • Primary Newspaper Proof: The New York Times (Tuesday, Nov 10, 1942, Radio Program): CBS / WABC at 9:30 PM lists Suspense thriller starring Michael Loring and Hans Conried.

  • Canonical Date: November 10, 1942

4. Box 13 — "The Great Meat Racket" (Dec 19, 1948)

  • Original Circulating Filename: Box_13_-_Episode_52_Dan_Holiday_Meat.mp3

  • Original Collector Label: Syndication Disc #52.

  • The Forensic Discovery: Alan Ladd as Dan Holiday replies to a classified ad placed in Box 13: "Trapped in black market meat packing ring."

  • Primary Newspaper Proof: Los Angeles Examiner (Sunday, Dec 19, 1948, Radio Highlights): Mutual syndication log lists episode #52 broadcast premiere.

  • Canonical Date: December 19, 1948

5. Escape — "The Blue Wall" (Nov 24, 1949)

  • Original Circulating Filename: Escape_-_Undated_Thanksgiving_Paul_Frees.mp3

  • Original Collector Label: Paul Frees Thanksgiving aircheck.

  • The Forensic Discovery: Paul Frees opens: "Tired of the everyday grind? Escape! Tonight we take you to the Andes Mountains and the mystery of The Blue Wall..."

  • Primary Newspaper Proof: The San Francisco Examiner (Thursday, Nov 24, 1949, Thanksgiving Radio Grid): CBS/KCQ lists Escape at 8:00 PM.

  • Canonical Date: November 24, 1949

items.title: Solving What Was "Lost to Time": How Audio AI and Primary Newspaper Scans Are Dating 76,000 Mystery Broadcasts
items.content_html:
A 70-Year Impasse in Broadcast History

For over half a century, the Old Time Radio (OTR) community has lived with a persistent frustration: thousands of surviving recordings have had no verified date or canonical identity.

Generations of collectors copied reel-to-reel tapes, transcribed disc matrix codes onto paper notebooks, and traded cassettes stamped with labels like:

  • "Date Unknown"

  • "19xx.xx.xx"

  • "The Part 12"

  • Completely blank filenames

Even the most dedicated historians could only cross-reference what was written on physical labels or indexed in hand-typed logs. If a disc label was missing, the episode's true identity remained "lost to time."

Why It Can Finally Be Solved Today

For the first time in archival history, we have united the four essential pillars required to solve these mysteries at scale:

  1. The Comprehensive Master Archive: 273,234 digitized historical recordings in our source-of-record catalog.

  2. Automated Neural Speech Recognition: Local Whisper ASR transcribing entire half-hour broadcasts in seconds, extracting every character name, villain alias, sponsor commercial, writer credit, and local station chime.

  3. Millions of Primary Newspaper Scans: Daily radio grids, "Today’s Radio Highlights" columns, and local station schedule pages from The New York Times, Los Angeles Times, Chicago Tribune, Detroit Free Press, San Francisco Chronicle, and regional dailies across America.

  4. Authoritative Master Network Logs: Master episode logs compiled by Jerry Haendiges (jjonez), J. David Goldin's lifelong radio database, and trade periodicals (Broadcasting, Billboard, Variety, Radio Mirror).

The "Smoking Gun" Method

The breakthrough comes when internal audio clues meet contemporary print verification:

[Spoken Audio Clue] ───➔ [Character / Sponsor / Station ID]
                               │
                               ▼
[Master Radio Log]  ───➔ [Potential Air Date Window]
                               │
                               ▼
[Morning Newspaper Scan] ➔ [Exact Station, Time Slot, and Highlight Blurb]
                               │
                               ▼
            ╔═══════════════════════════════════╗
            ║ 100% CANONICAL HISTORICAL MATCH   ║
            ╚═══════════════════════════════════╝

Example: The "Lost" Gunsmoke Blood Feud

For 70 years, a classic Gunsmoke recording circulated among collectors as an undated mystery labeled "Ambush at Medicine Lodge".

  • Audio Clue: Our ASR transcription caught Matt Dillon mediating a blood feud between the Peavey and Cade families in the Gypsum Hills, followed by a CBS promo for the television program Mr. Citizen (hosted by Allyn Edwards in spring 1955).

  • Newspaper Proof: April 16, 1955 newspaper radio grids confirmed the broadcast of "The Gypsum Hills Feud" (Episode #157).

A Permanent Record for the Public

Every resolved broadcast is immediately restored in our catalog, added to its exact day in the 365-day calendar (/catalog/{month}-{day}), equipped with synchronized WebVTT captions in R2, and durably recorded in our public progress ledger.

We are turning thousands of forgotten recordings into an open, searchable, and dated record of 20th-century cultural history.
